title: Slideshow wallpaper changes when turning off and on the monitor, even if this would be too early based on the chosen switching frequency
line: A slideshow wallpaper keeps its current image when a monitor is turned off and on, until its interval is over.
explanation: Reconnecting a screen destroys and recreates its wallpaper, and the slideshow's timing only lived in memory. On start, random order always began a fresh shuffle and showed a new image, however long the interval. The change saves when the slideshow picked its image (SlideChangeTime, next to Image) and, when the wallpaper starts again within the same interval, shows the saved image and only starts the timer; otherwise it moves on to the next slide as before.

commits.message:
wallpapers/image: Keep the slideshow image within its interval

The wallpaper is recreated when a screen is reconnected, so a random
slideshow picked a new image at once. Save when the image was picked and,
if that is still in the current interval, show it again and keep waiting.

BUG: 491002

media.caption: Master: second output with a random slideshow (1 h interval), before and after 3 unplug/replug cycles: a new image each time
With the fix: same setup and 3 replugs, the image stays the same

review.text: Clean, minimal fix in plasma-workspace that persists SlideChangeTime alongside Image and keeps the saved wallpaper when recreated within the same epoch-aligned slideshow interval. Both random and ordered slideshows are handled properly without duplicate transitions on reshuffle, and the before/after screenshots and autotest runs convincingly verify the fix.

reviews.text: Clean, minimal fix in plasma-workspace that persists SlideChangeTime alongside Image and keeps the saved wallpaper when recreated within the same epoch-aligned slideshow interval. Both random and ordered slideshows are handled properly without duplicate transitions on reshuffle, and the before/after screenshots and autotest runs convincingly verify the fix.

This implements what Marco suggested in c3: the slideshow saves when it picked its image (SlideChangeTime next to Image) and, when the wallpaper is recreated on a screen reconnect within the same epoch-aligned interval that scheduleNextSlide() already uses, restores that slide and only reschedules the timer. Splitting scheduleNextSlide() out of nextSlide() is clean, the QML writeImageConfig signature matches the new Q_ARG(double), and the kcfg entry is added only where slideshow mode writes it. The 4-shot grids prove it for the reported random/long-interval case, and the 60 s and alphabetical checks cover regressions. The disclosed behaviour change (no new random image at a login within the same interval; ordered slideshows move on once the interval has passed) fits the user's chosen interval and is reasonable.
